title: Operator Briefs — condensed operator profiles (sketch)
content:
Context / motivation:
- Problem: product teams keep asking for a compact way to describe desired agent behaviour and resource budget to the inference layer. Long prompts or full policy documents are heavy and error-prone for day-to-day product changes.
- Idea: small "operator briefs" — concise JSON-ish profiles that capture intent, fidelity, token budget, safety posture, and fallback preferences. Meant to be authored quickly by PMs/PDs and read by runtime for routing/quality decisions.

Goals:
- Make it trivial to change behavior across a fleet of assistants without rewriting prompts.
- Expose a tiny surface area (3-7 fields) that map cleanly to runtime knobs (model variant, quantization, batching lane, prefix cache).
- Keep authoring approachable for non-LLM engineers; defaults do the heavy lifting.

Constraints / non-goals:
- Not a replacement for full policy or persona systems. This is tactical and lightweight.
- Should not leak PII or secrets — enforced by authoring UI + validation.
- Initially only for Hosted and Dedicated; Private later if adoption justifies additional schema fields for compliance.

Operator brief sketch (proto fields):
- id: human-friendly short string (e.g., "helpdesk-summary")
- intent: short description (1 line) for humans and for feature discovery
- fidelity: low|medium|high (maps to model size + sampling settings)
- token_budget: integer (soft guidance for collector/response length)
- safety_tier: permissive|balanced|strict (toggle model filters + post-checks)
- fallback_policy: prefer-smaller-model|soft-degrade|failover-to-search
- metrics_kpis: comma list (latency_p50, summary_coherence, cost_per_1k)
- tags: freeform

Example (informal):
{
  id: "hd-summary-compact",
  intent: "Condense customer message thread into 3 bullets + action items",
  fidelity: "medium",
  token_budget: "160",
  safety_tier: "balanced",
  fallback_policy: "prefer-smaller-model",
  metrics_kpis: "latency_p95,summary_f1,cost_per_1k",
  tags: "helpdesk,recap,default"
}

How this plugs into runtime (rough):
- On request: client includes operator_brief_id (optional). If present, router resolves to a profile -> maps to model family, max tokens, sampling params, and a cost bucket.
- Runtime applies KV/prefix caching rules based on intent (e.g., templates for summaries use cached prompt chunks).
- Observability: brief_id shows up in Console with cost/latency and quality evals.

User stories (short):
- PM: "As a PM I want to flip fidelity to low for a set of flows so we can save cost during black-friday traffic spikes."
- SRE: "As SRE I want to route operator briefs with high latency sensitivity to the low-latency pool."
- CS: "As CS I want a default brief for outbound summaries so we reduce manual prompt edits."

Experiment ideas:
- A/B: map existing summary flows to operator briefs vs present-day prompts and compare cost & coherence over 2w.
- Auto-suggest: when a user creates a brief, suggest fidelity/token_budget by sampling 5 recent requests and simulating cost.
- Fallback stress test: intentionally saturate primary pool and observe production fallback behavior for different fallback_policy values.

Metrics to track:
- adoption_rate (percent of flows using briefs)
- avg_cost_delta (compared to baseline prompts)
- quality_delta (summary_coherence/acceptance rate)
- authoring_time (seconds to create brief in UI)

Open questions / design notes:
- Should briefs allow per-route overrides (e.g., different token_budget for edges)? Might add a small map field but risk complexity.
- How to present briefs in Console so non-technical users can safely toggle fidelity? (slider + recommended impact preview?)
- Backwards compatibility: when we change fidelity mappings, we need rollouts with read-only migration.
- Validation: enforce token_budget <= model max, safety_tier mapping must include a whitelist of allowed post-checks.

Risks:
- PMs misuse brief to ask for too-aggressive cost cuts that degrade UX. Need guardrails + experiments.
- Explosion of briefs (fragmentation) — require naming conventions + visibility.

Next steps / quick action list (personal):
- Draft a minimal JSON schema and example mapping table of fidelity -> model/config (1 day).
- Wire a tiny backend mock that returns profile->serving config (2 days) to demo to Eng infra.
- Run a 1-week internal pilot: pick 3 flows (helpdesk recap, onboarding email draft, search-summary) and convert to briefs.
- Surface brief_id in Console trace view and add a simple cost preview tool (spike).

Notes to self:
- Talk to Ravi about Console affordances (Feb sync).
- Check with Legal if safety_tier labels have any compliance implications.
- Keep schema intentionally limited; extend after pilot.

Scratchpad prompts / utility snippets to test quickly via curl:
- curl -X POST /v1/generate -d '{"brief_id":"hd-summary-compact","input":"..."}' -> measure tokens
- generator: run sanity comparisons with top-3 model variants to calibrate fidelity mapping

Mini UX sketch (very rough):
- Authoring modal: Title, One-line intent, Fidelity (3 buttons with tooltip), Token budget (slider + suggested), Safety tier dropdown, Save as draft
- Console: list of briefs with usage bars + cost estimate button

Links / references to keep in mind:
- Prior compact-recap notes (see: CONFLUENCE-REC-341)
- Cost ladder fallback work from Sam (JIRA INF-998)

End of sketch. This is intentionally thin — want to iterate quickly and show a demo before formalizing schema.

Random parking-lot thoughts (one-liners):
- Could tie briefs to feature flags so we can safely roll them out per-customer
- Consider simple templating: briefs can include a short template id that the runtime expands from a template store
- Maybe provide 'suggested_briefs' from historical telemetry (auto-surface candidates)
summary: Personal scratchpad for a lightweight 'operator briefs' concept: minimal metadata profiles that map product intent to runtime serving knobs. Draft includes proto schema, UX/experiments, metrics, open questions, and next steps.
